name: Ruby
summary: Work with Ruby values, hashes, enumerable collections, objects, and validated line input.

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
Install a supported Ruby runtime to run the examples from a terminal with ruby lesson.rb. These examples also run with Ruby 2.6 syntax.
metadata.miniProject: Build a reading tracker. Parse pages from input lines, keep a count by category, and print a sorted report. Report each invalid line and keep processing later lines.

lessons.title: Values, defaults, and interpolation
lessons.explanation: A Ruby variable can refer to any kind of value. Interpolate an expression inside a double-quoted string. The || operator returns its right operand when the left operand is nil or false.
lessons.example:
subject = "systems"
pages = 12
edition = nil
label = edition || "draft"
puts "#{subject}: #{pages} pages (#{label})"

api.name: puts
api.description: Print a value followed by a newline.

api.name: #{expression}
api.description: Insert the result of an expression into a double-quoted string.

api.name: nil
api.description: Represent the absence of a value.

lessons.practice: Display the title and total pages of two readings. Print "untitled" when a title is nil.
lessons.pitfall: An empty string and zero are truthy in Ruby. Use empty? or a numeric comparison when those values need special handling.

exercise.expected: Produce one formatted line for each reading and a meaningful label when its title is missing.
exercise.completion: The missing title prints "untitled", and a reading with zero pages still prints 0.

lessons.title: Count occurrences with a hash
lessons.explanation: A hash maps keys to values. Hash.new(0) supplies zero when a lookup finds no entry. Assign the incremented count back to the hash. Sorting the keys gives the report an explicit order.
lessons.example:
topics = ["arrays", "loops", "arrays"]
counts = Hash.new(0)
topics.each do |topic|
  counts[topic] += 1
end

counts.keys.sort.each do |topic|
  puts "#{topic}: #{counts[topic]}"
end

api.name: Hash.new(0)
api.description: Return zero for a missing key without creating an entry.

api.name: each do |item|
api.description: Call a block with each value in a collection.

api.name: Hash#keys
api.description: Return an array of stored keys.

lessons.practice: Count categories for ["review", "read", "review", "run"]. Print the counts in alphabetical order.
lessons.pitfall: A mutable object passed as the hash default is shared by missing lookups. For arrays per key, use a block that creates a fresh array.

exercise.expected: Print one line per distinct category with its frequency.
exercise.completion: The report contains read: 1, review: 2, and run: 1 in that order.

lessons.title: Filter and transform a collection
lessons.explanation: Enumerable supplies operations over collections that implement each. Use select when a block decides which elements to keep. Use map when a block creates a new value from each element.

api.name: select
api.description: Return the elements that satisfy a condition.

api.name: map
api.description: Return the values produced by a block.

api.name: sum
api.description: Add the values in a numeric collection.

lessons.practice: Keep the even entries from [1, 8, 3, 6], double them, and print the new list and total.
lessons.pitfall: Use each for a side effect such as printing. Use map when you need the collected results.

exercise.expected: Filter first, transform the filtered values, and sum the results.
exercise.completion: The transformed values are 16 and 12. The total is 28.

lessons.title: Store related state in an object
lessons.explanation: A class defines methods and per-object state. initialize prepares a newly created instance. Variables whose names start with @ belong to that instance. An attr_reader exposes a read method for a field.

api.name: class
api.description: Define a set of methods for objects.

api.name: initialize
api.description: Initialize state for an instance created with new.

api.name: attr_reader
api.description: Generate a read method for an instance variable.

lessons.practice: Add a withdraw method that rejects amounts above the balance. Confirm that the balance is preserved after a rejected withdrawal.
lessons.pitfall: Keep changes that must obey a rule behind a method. A publicly writable field can bypass that rule.

exercise.expected: Withdraw valid amounts and report an error for insufficient funds.
exercise.completion: A withdrawal of 100 from 325 gives 225. A later withdrawal of 500 leaves 225.

lessons.title: Parse and validate input line by line
lessons.explanation: Read input one line at a time and convert each line with Integer. Pass a base of ten when you expect decimal input. Rescue the conversion failure and keep processing later lines. StringIO lets this example use an in-memory input stream.
lessons.example:
require "stringio"

input = StringIO.new("12\nunknown\n5\n")
total = 0
input.each_line do |line|
  begin
    total += Integer(line.strip, 10)
  rescue ArgumentError
    puts "invalid: #{line.strip}"
  end
end
puts "total: #{total}"

api.name: each_line
api.description: Iterate over lines from an IO-like input.

api.name: Integer(text, 10)
api.description: Parse text as a base-ten integer.

api.name: rescue ArgumentError
api.description: Handle invalid text while allowing unrelated exceptions to propagate.

lessons.practice: Sum nonnegative integers from a line stream. Report malformed or negative lines and keep going.
lessons.pitfall: String#to_i can return zero for malformed text. Use Integer when invalid input must be reported separately.

exercise.expected: Print one error for each rejected line and a total for accepted readings.
exercise.completion: Input 3, -1, x, and 7 produces two errors and a total of 10.
